([[Putnam, Connecticut]]) | college = * [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2022–2024) * [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] (2024–2025) * [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] (2025–2026) | highlights = * [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Defensive team (2026) }} '''Ugonna Kingsley Onyenso''' {{Audio|Ig-Ugonna Kingsley Onyenso.ogg|Listen|help=no}} (born 25 September 2004) is a Nigerian [[college basketball]] player for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]] of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). He previously played for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]] and [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State Wildcats]]. He also plays for the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team|Nigeria national team]], where he was the youngest player to ever play for the team at age 17. Standing at 7 ft 0 in (2.11 m){{Cite web |date=2022-08-26 |title=Ugonna Onyenso |url=https://ukathletics.com/roster/ugonna-kingsley-onyenso/ |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=UK Athletics |language=en-US}} with a wing span of 7 ft 5 in (2.26 m), he plays the [[center (basketball)|center]] position. == Early career == Born in [[Owerri]], Onyenso played football as a kid before a local coach proposed playing basketball to him.{{Cite web |date=2022-02-26 |title=Ugonna Kingsley Onyenso: The journey so far |url=https://afroballers.com/ugonna-kingsley-onyenso-the-journey-so-far/ |access-date=2022-08-02 |website=Afroballers |language=en-US}} Kingsley was a student-athlete at the [[NBA Academy Africa]] in [[Thiès]], Senegal, where he played for three years.{{Cite news |last=Abayomi |first=Tosin |date=2022-08-02 |title=D'Tigers star Kingsley Onyenso signs for Kentucky |url=https://www.pulse.ng/sports/other-sports/ugonna-kingsley-onyenso-joins-kentucky-wildcats/xxnm9l0 |access-date=2022-08-02 |newspaper=[[Pulse Nigeria]]|language=en}} In January 2021, he moved to the United States to play for the Putnam Science Academy in [[Putnam, Connecticut]]. With Putnam, Onyenso averaged 13.2 points, 9.2 rebounds and 2.7 blocks per game as the team went 20-0 during his tenure there. In August 2021, he also played for Team England of the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU). He played in the 2022 NBA Academy Games and averaged 13.2 points, 9.2 rebounds and 2.7 blocks per game. == College career == On August 2, 2022, Onyenso committed to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], choosing them over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] and [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]].{{Cite web |last=Tristan |first=Pharis |date=2022-08-01 |title=5-star center Ugonna Kingsley commits to Kentucky |url=https://www.aseaofblue.com/2022/8/1/23269407/ugonna-kingsley-kentucky-basketball-2022-recruits |access-date=2022-08-02 |website=A Sea Of Blue |language=en}} He played sparingly as a freshman. Onyenso missed the first month on his sophomore season with a foot injury but averaged 3.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.8 blocked shots per game. Following the season, he entered the [[2024 NBA draft]] before withdrawing and transferring to [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]].{{cite news |last1=Drummond |first1=Cameron |title=After planning to turn pro, former Kentucky player Ugonna Onyenso transfers to a new school |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article287944175.html |access-date=December 20, 2025 |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |date=June 4, 2024}} Onyenso averaged 2.8 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 0.9 blocks per game for Kansas State. He entered the transfer portal again after the season, ultimately landing at [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]].{{cite news |last1=Franciulli |first1=Jacquie |title=Kansas State center Ugonna Onyenso will transfer to Virginia |url=https://247sports.com/college/virginia/article/kansas-state-center-ugonna-onyenso-will-transfer-to-virginia--249172078/ |access-date=December 20, 2025 |work=247 Sports |date=April 30, 2025}} == National team career == In November 2021, Onyenso was selected for the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team|Nigeria national senior team]] by coach [[Julius Nwosu]]. In his debut, he scored 10 points, four rebounds and two blocks in 16 minutes against [[Uganda men's national basketball team|Uganda]]. At age 17, he became the youngest player in history to play for the Nigerian national team. == Personal life == Onyenso is the son of Martins and Lilian Chinyere, and he has four siblings. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://virginiasports.com/sports/mbball/roster/season/2025-26/player/ugonna-onyenso/ Virginia Cavaliers bio] *[https://www.kstatesports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/ugonna-onyenso/12180 Kansas State Wildcats bio] *[https://ukathletics.com/sports/mbball/roster/player/ugonna-kingsley-onyenso/ Kentucky Wildcats bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Onyenson, Ugonna}} [[Category:2004 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century Nigerian sportsmen]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball players]] [[Category:Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball players]] [[Category:NBA Academy Africa players]] [[Category:Nigerian expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Nigerian men's basketball players]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Owerri]] [[Category:Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball players]]
